dedupe_keys.name: nasa aviation safety reporting system asrs database

description: The Aviation Safety Reporting System (ASRS), run by NASA, collects confidential voluntary safety reports from aviation's frontline personnel, among them pilots, air traffic controllers, mechanics, flight attendants and dispatchers, analyses them and shares the lessons with the aviation community. NASA calls its database the world's largest repository of such voluntary, confidential safety information. Each record holds the reporter's narrative, sanitised of identifying details, and information coded by expert analysts for retrieval and analysis. ASRS Database Online allows searches whose results can be viewed as HTML or exported to Word, Excel or CSV, one row per incident and up to 10,000 records per export. ASRS also publishes the free monthly CALLBACK newsletter and a newsletter on drones. Coverage: reports from the US aviation system. Format and access: an online search and export tool, free and without registration. Licence and cost: US government information; no licence is stated. Caveats: NASA does not verify or validate reports, and voluntary reporting is not a random sample, so counts do not measure rates. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of near misses and human factors in aviation. It complements the FAA ASIAS data and the NTSB CAROL investigations in the catalogue.
